question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III) observes a stock-swap merger: Acquirer ACQ trades at INR 600 and Target TGT trades at INR 45. Conversion ratio announced: 130 TGT shares per 10 ACQ shares. What is the FAIR price of ACQ implied by the conversion ratio (using TGT market price)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Fair price of Acquirer = (Conversion ratio numerator * Target price) / Conversion ratio denominator = (130 * 45) / 10 = 5850/10 = INR 585.00. ACQ at INR 600 is OVER-valued relative to the implied swap — so the arb is SHORT ACQ / LONG TGT. The Trap: Option B is the market price, not the fair price. Option C swaps numerator-denominator. Option D inverts the ratio entirely. Cross-Exam Context: Same formula as PDF Example 10.7. XIX-C covers identically. XV (Research Analyst) derives the conversion ratio from intrinsic-value work. Manager's Pro-Tip: Factor in deal-break probability: spread you capture = (Acquirer offer - Target price) * P(deal closes) - deal-break downside * P(break). Cat III merger-arb sleeves typically require >90% deal-completion odds; anything below is 'situation' — move to event-driven desk.
